title: BridgeTwist: Twisting Schrödinger Bridges for Training-Free Conditional Sampling
topic: Probabilistic Methods->Monte Carlo and Sampling Methods
claim: A sampler propagates weighted particles through repeated propose, reweight and resample steps, guided by endpoint-based likelihoods and time-varying schedules.
layout: Top row of three inset panels feeding a bottom left-to-right particle timeline with loop arrow
description: The figure has two rows. The top row has three boxes. The left box, "Endpoint prediction", shows velocity and score arrows from a state x_t pointing to a predicted endpoint. The middle box is a magenta "Observation y" box with an arrow to a "Tempered likelihood" box. The right box is a small plot of the likelihood-tempering schedule β(t), a rising line, and the proposal-noise schedule g(t), a dashed arch. Dashed arrows link these boxes down to the main row. The bottom row is a left-to-right particle flow from Source (t0=0) through ellipsis and branching or dying particles to Current particles at t_n. A highlighted teal panel, "One SMC update", shows Proposal, Reweight (circle size is weight) and Resample columns. The row ends at Posterior (t_N=1), with a loop arrow reading "Repeat for n=0,…,N−1". Colors are teal, navy and magenta.
caption: \ours{} overview. Schr\"odinger bridge's velocity and score predict endpoints for likelihood evaluation. The schedules $\beta(t)$ and $g(t)$ control likelihood tempering and proposal noise, respectively. Vertical position denotes state and circle area denotes weight. Resampling copies retain their states and are offset horizontally for visibility. The highlighted SMC update repeats along the time grid, and the terminal weighted particles approximate the target conditional distribution.
abstract: Generative models are often required to serve many downstream conditional tasks. In the training-free setting, a pretrained unconditional model is reused as a prior and combined with a task-specific likelihood to sample from the corresponding posterior. While such training-free samplers have been developed for diffusion and flow models, their counterpart for SchrÃ¶dinger bridge (SB) models remains unexplored, despite the growing appeal of SBs as flexible stochastic transport models between general source and target distributions. We propose BridgeTwist, a training-free conditional sampler for pretrained SB generative models, formulated as a tempered twisted sequential Monte Carlo scheme. The twist function employs a plug-in surrogate built on a closed-form endpoint predictor, which is derived by combining the velocity and score fields obtained from the SB pretraining. Since this surrogate is less reliable near the source, we temper the twist function with a time-varying exponent, downweighting its influence at early steps. We further introduce a bridge-shaped inference-time diffusion schedule that concentrates the proposal noise in the interior of the path. Telescoping importance weights then cancel all intermediate twist factors, yielding an asymptotically exact sampler for the posterior. Empirically, BridgeTwist outperforms training-free baselines on class-conditional and text-prompted image generation, and is competitive with specialized inverse problem solvers on inpainting, deblurring, and super-resolution.
